description: Advanced Research Computing (ARC), a division of U-M's Information and Technology Services, offers scientific computing and research consulting to help researchers implement machine learning and data-driven workflows. ARC provides expert guidance on data science projects, helps identify the right tools, and supports programming for advanced analytics, machine learning, and computational techniques, distinct from general HPC usage support.
category: Computing & Technical Resources; Consulting & Support

resource_name: Data Science for Dynamic Intervention Decision Making Center (d3)
description: The Data Science for Dynamic Intervention Decision Making Center (d3) develops the methodological toolkit scientists need to address major public health challenges. d3 collaborates with and trains scientific partners worldwide to implement its methodology, catalyzing a new generation of evidence-based, technology-powered treatments that improve health and education outcomes.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Consulting & Support

resource_name: Statistical Analysis of Biomedical and Educational Research Group (SABER)
description: The Statistical Analysis of Biomedical and Educational Research Group (SABER), a unit of the Department of Biostatistics, provides expertise in the design, conduct, and analysis of multi-center clinical trials and multidisciplinary research. SABER has served as the data coordinating center for numerous NIH-funded and industry-sponsored studies, bringing biostatistical design and analysis expertise to a wide range of health-related research.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Consulting & Support

resource_name: Clinical & Health Research Dissemination & Implementation Science Catalyst (DISC)
description: DISC manages several dissemination and implementation (D&I) science resources for U-M study teams, including the Implementation Science Network (ISN), which builds a community of faculty, staff, and trainees interested in D&I research. DISC also provides training resources, a works-in-progress series for investigators, and expert consultations.
category: Funding & Project Development

description: e-HAIL is a joint initiative between the College of Engineering and Michigan Medicine that builds faculty community and supports grant development through innovation in AI and health.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Funding & Project Development

description: AI & Digital Health Innovation (AI&DHI) provides U-M researchers with the tools to develop and implement clinical AI models and AI-based technologies that enhance digital healthcare. By convening interdisciplinary teams of health providers, scientists, engineers, and administrators, AI&DHI helps investigators tackle difficult research problems and rapidly bring solutions to the bedside.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Computing & Technical Resources; Funding & Project Development

description: The Michigan Alzheimer's Disease Center (MADC) is a National Institute on Aging-designated center focused on research into Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Beyond advancing research, MADC serves investigators and the public by offering clinical studies and research registries, support with diagnosis and medical management, disease information, and support groups.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research

description: Since 1988, the Michigan AI Lab has advanced foundational AI research that shapes the future of intelligent systems. category: AI Development; Research & Methods; Consulting & Support

resource_name: Michigan Institute for Computational Discovery & Engineering
description: MICDE is the University of Michigan's hub for computational science and engineering, advancing research and education at the intersection of scientific computing, AI, and high-performance computing. It connects researchers across disciplines and offers research and educational programs, events, and collaborative opportunities that accelerate computational and AI-for-science innovation.
category: AI Development; Research & Methods; Computing & Technical Resources

description: The Arts Research: Incubation & Acceleration (ARIA) program, a joint effort between the U-M Arts Initiative and the Office of the Vice President for Research, supports projects that expand arts research and creative practice across campus. ARIA encourages interdisciplinary research teams and individuals in creative practice to pursue new collaborations and new artistic and scholarly horizons.
category: Arts, Humanities & Creative Practice; Funding & Project Development

description: The Center for Global Health Equity champions collaborative efforts to address health disparities in resource-constrained settings worldwide. Based at the University of Michigan, the Center integrates co-design principles across research, training, and policy translation to produce solutions that are equitable, evidence-based, and built to last.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Ethics, Society & Policy

resource_name: Michigan Center for Applied and Interdisciplinary Mathematics
description: Founded in 2016, the Michigan Center for Applied and Interdisciplinary Mathematics (MCAIM) serves as a campus-wide hub for applied and interdisciplinary mathematics at the University of Michigan. MCAIM brings together researchers from across campus, including mathematicians, scientists, and engineers, to catalyze new collaborations, identify emerging research directions, and advance discoveries made possible through shared expertise.
category: AI Research; Development & Methods; Consulting & Support

description: Bold Challenges, an Office of the Vice President for Research initiative, leads events and programs that empower researchers to build dynamic teams, produce transformative discoveries, and improve quality of life for communities across the state, nation, and world. It increases cross-school collaboration, forecasts funding opportunities, and offers broad, inclusive pathways to large-scale external research funding.
category: Funding & Project Development

resource_name: Center for Ethics, Society, and Computing (ESC)
description: The Center for Ethics, Society, and Computing (ESC) intervenes when digital media and computing technologies reproduce inequality, exclusion, corruption, deception, racism, or sexism. A research center and collective of scholars, ESC takes feminist, justice-focused, and interdisciplinary approaches to computing, working with educators, workers, industry practitioners, and policymakers on the social, cultural, and political dimensions of digital technology.
category: Ethics, Society & Policy; Applied & Domain Focused Research

description: The Digital Studies Institute is a center for research and dialogue where faculty, students, and visitors examine technology, digital culture, and social justice. Questions about the impact of technology on race, disability, gender, sexuality, class, power, and identity are central to its undergraduate minor, graduate concentration, annual summer institute, and public programs. DSI is also home to the DISCO Network research initiative.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research; Ethics, Society & Policy; Arts, Humanities & Creative Practice

resource_name: Science, Technology, and Public Policy (STPP) Program
description: The Science, Technology, and Public Policy (STPP) Program advances social equity and justice in the governance of science and technology through education, research, and policy engagement. Its AI-focused work spans student training on AI's societal impacts, research on AI's social and justice implications, and partnerships that equip non-profits, government agencies, and advocacy organizations to make informed AI decisions.

resource_name: Michigan Institute for Data & AI in Society
description: The Michigan Institute for Data & AI in Society (MIDAS) advances data science and AI to achieve lasting scientific and societal impact. With more than 700 affiliated faculty and a community of over 1,000 students and postdocs across 70 campus units, MIDAS is one of the largest data science and AI institutes at a U.S. university, offering a broad portfolio of research, training, and partnership programs.
category: AI Research; Development & Methods; Consulting & Support

category: AI Development; Research & Methods; Consulting & Support

description: The Human Centered Computing (HCC) Lab at the University of Michigan investigates human-computer interaction (HCI), educational technology, multimedia, and social computing. Its faculty cover a broad range of HCI topics, from foundational research to emerging technologies and services.
category: AI Research

resource_name: Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship
description: The Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship, funded by Schmidt Sciences, gives outstanding early-career researchers intensive training in applying AI methodologies to scientific research. The program catalyzes transformative AI-driven scientific breakthroughs, helps the broader U-M research community adopt AI across science and engineering, and collaborates with other sites to maximize impact.
category: Funding & Project Development

description: The University of Michigan Center for Academic Innovation (CAI) brings educational opportunities to a global network of lifelong learners through curricular innovation and learning technologies. CAI offers learning experience design, educational technology platforms like Atlas, and integration of AI and extended-reality tools into teaching. It also provides policy guidance on digital privacy, vendor licensing, and analytics data governance.
category: Consulting & Support

description: Deep Blue Repositories give the University of Michigan community safe, durable access to the research, teaching, learning, and creative work that makes U-M a leader in these areas, whether that work takes the form of documents or data.
category: Computing & Technical Resources

category: Research & Methods

description: The Robotics Department at the University of Michigan develops the next generation of robotics and roboticists as force-multipliers for society. category: Applied & Domain Focused Research

description: Mcity operates a world-class test facility with mixed-reality testing capabilities, a data engine, and renowned talent, serving as the University of Michigan's hub for research, development, and deployment of next-generation mobility innovations.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research

Its faculty are renowned researchers and educators working on some of today's most relevant problems, training the next generation of leaders in the field.

Its faculty, students, and staff bring biostatistical design and analysis expertise to a wide range of health research, including clinical trials, machine learning, statistical genetics, and survival analysis.
category: Research & Methods

description: The Gilbert S. Omenn Department of Computational Medicine and Bioinformatics (DCMB) advances the understanding of biological mechanisms and accelerates biomedical discovery and translational research. DCMB develops computational and biomedical data science methods, including novel AI and machine learning approaches, while training the next generation of innovators in an interdisciplinary research culture.
category: Applied & Domain Focused Research

description: The Department of Learning Health Sciences (DLHS) is a first-in-the-nation basic science department focused on the sciences of learning across individual, group, organizational, regional, and national scales. DLHS works to improve health by advancing the sciences that make learning effective, routine, and efficient, pursuing three goals: advancing research, providing education, and offering service programs.

resource_name: Trust, Innovation & Ethics Research for Responsible AI (TIERRA)
description: TIERRA is a collaborative space that harnesses the knowledge and influence of health AI stakeholders. Drawing on the expertise of academic faculty and students, industry professionals, policymakers, and community members, TIERRA creates collaborations, research, roadmaps, and resources that inform best practices and policies for developing and applying AI in healthcare.
category: Ethics, Society & Policy

resource_name: Center for Data-Driven Drug Development and Treatment Assessment (DATA)
description: The Center for Data-Driven Drug Development and Treatment Assessment (DATA) aims to strengthen the national research infrastructure and grow the engineering and scientific workforce through its research. DATA develops new methodologies for industry-wide collaborative drug discovery to reduce costs and speed new medicines, focusing on machine learning for drug discovery, a secure data hub for pharmaceutical and patient data, and privacy-preserving federated learning across encrypted databases.
category: AI Research; Applied & Domain Focused Research

resource_name: Center for Prediction, Reasoning & Intelligence for Multiphysics Exploration (C-PRIME)
description: C-PRIME aims to revolutionize predictive science by uncovering how small-scale physics shapes emergent behavior across complex physical systems, using a rotating detonation combustor as its target application. The center develops autonomous AI agents and new algorithms to systematically refine combinations of physics, simulations, and computing infrastructure, shrinking the time from scientific inquiry to actionable predictive insight.
category: AI Research; Applied & Domain Focused Research
thematic_area: Physical Sciences & Engineering; AI & Machine Learning

description: The Center for Complex Particle Systems (COMPASS) creates, measures, and models complex materials by combining molecular, nano-, and microscale components. By integrating order and disorder, COMPASS develops simple chemical pathways toward sustainable, multifunctional, intelligent materials, bridging graph theory, network physics, and particle science to address technological, medical, and environmental challenges.
category: AI Research; Applied & Domain Focused Research
